USA.fact: Federal debt held by the public now roughly equals the size of the entire US economy.

CHN.fact: China's population has shrunk every year since 2022 as births fall to record lows.

JPN.fact: Nearly 30 percent of Japanese are aged 65 or older, the highest share of any major country.

DEU.fact: Germany's economy shrank in both 2023 and 2024, its first back-to-back contraction in two decades.

IND.fact: India overtook China as the world's most populous country in 2023, with over 1.4 billion people.

GBR.fact: The UK imports around 40 percent of the food it eats.

FRA.tagline: Land of nuclear power and wine
FRA.fact: France gets about two thirds of its electricity from nuclear power, the highest share in the world.

ITA.fact: Italy's public debt is about 135 percent of GDP, among the highest in Europe.

CAN.fact: About three quarters of Canada's exports go to the United States.

BRA.fact: Brazil is the world's largest exporter of soybeans, coffee, beef and sugar.

RUS.tagline: The world's largest country by area
RUS.fact: Oil and gas taxes provide roughly a quarter to a third of Russia's federal budget revenue.

KOR.fact: South Korea has the world's lowest fertility rate, around 0.75 children per woman in 2024.

AUS.fact: Australia supplies more than half of the world's seaborne iron ore.

ESP.fact: Spain welcomed a record 94 million international tourists in 2024, second only to France.

MEX.fact: More than 80 percent of Mexico's exports go to the United States.

IDN.fact: Indonesia holds the world's largest nickel reserves and has banned raw ore exports to build smelters.

TUR.fact: Turkish inflation peaked above 75 percent in 2024 before easing to around 33 percent in 2025.

NLD.fact: About a quarter of the Netherlands lies below sea level, protected by dikes and dunes.

SAU.fact: Saudi Arabia aims to cut oil dependence under Vision 2030, funding megaprojects like NEOM.

CHE.fact: Switzerland has kept armed neutrality since 1815 and remains outside both the EU and NATO.

POL.fact: Poland spends over 4 percent of GDP on defence, the highest share in NATO.

TWN.tagline: Maker of the world's best chips
TWN.fact: Taiwan's TSMC makes over 90 percent of the world's most advanced chips.

BEL.fact: Antwerp-Bruges is Europe's second-largest port and its largest chemical cluster.

SWE.fact: Sweden joined NATO in March 2024, ending two centuries of military non-alignment.

ARG.tagline: Farm powerhouse riding boom and bust
ARG.fact: Argentina's annual inflation fell from nearly 300 percent in 2024 to around 30 percent by late 2025.

IRL.fact: Corporation tax, mostly from a few US multinationals, makes up about a quarter of Ireland's tax revenue.

ISR.fact: Israel spends more on research and development relative to GDP than any other country, about 6 percent.

SGP.fact: Singapore imports over 90 percent of its food and buys part of its water from Malaysia.

ARE.tagline: Desert hub of trade and finance
ARE.fact: About nine in ten residents of the UAE are foreign nationals.

THA.fact: Thailand is one of the world's top rice exporters and Southeast Asia's largest car producer.

AUT.fact: Hydropower supplies around 60 percent of Austria's electricity.

NOR.tagline: Oil wealth with a green conscience
NOR.fact: Norway's sovereign wealth fund, the world's largest, is worth about 20 trillion kroner.

PHL.tagline: Island nation powered by its people
PHL.fact: The Philippines is now the world's largest rice importer.

VNM.fact: Vietnam runs the third-largest trade surplus with the United States, after China and Mexico.

BGD.fact: Ready-made garments make up over 80 percent of Bangladesh's export earnings.

IRN.fact: Tehran faced severe water shortages in 2025 as reservoirs fell to record lows after years of drought.

DNK.fact: Wind turbines generate over half of Denmark's electricity.

MYS.tagline: Chips, palm oil and twin towers
MYS.fact: Malaysia is one of the world's largest semiconductor back-end hubs, handling about 13 percent of global chip assembly and testing.

HKG.fact: Hong Kong imports over 90 percent of its food, mostly from mainland China.

COL.fact: Colombia is the world's largest producer of washed arabica coffee and second-largest exporter of cut flowers.

ZAF.fact: South Africa's unemployment rate is above 30 percent, one of the highest in the world.

ROU.tagline: Black Sea economy on the rise
ROU.fact: Romania ran the EU's largest budget deficit in 2024, at over 9 percent of GDP.

EGY.fact: Suez Canal revenue fell by more than half in 2024 as Houthi attacks diverted shipping.

PAK.fact: Pakistan has needed over 20 IMF bailouts, most recently a 7 billion dollar programme agreed in 2024.

CHL.fact: Chile produces about a quarter of the world's copper.

CZE.fact: Czechia builds about 1.4 million cars a year, one of the highest rates per person in the world.

NGA.fact: Nigeria's Dangote refinery, Africa's largest, aims to end the country's reliance on imported petrol.

FIN.fact: Finland shares a 1,340 km border with Russia and joined NATO in 2023.

PRT.fact: Portugal produces about half of the world's cork.

KAZ.tagline: Central Asia's oil and uranium giant
KAZ.fact: Kazakhstan is the world's largest uranium producer, mining about 40 percent of the global supply.

PER.tagline: Andean land of copper and gold
PER.fact: Peru is the world's largest exporter of blueberries and a top producer of copper, silver and zinc.

IRQ.fact: Oil provides about 90 percent of Iraq's government revenue.

DZA.tagline: Africa's largest country, rich in gas
DZA.fact: Hydrocarbons make up over 90 percent of Algeria's export earnings.

NZL.fact: New Zealand is the world's largest exporter of dairy products, which earn about a quarter of its goods exports.

GRC.tagline: Ancient democracy with a shipping empire
GRC.fact: Greek shipowners control the world's largest merchant fleet, about a fifth of global tonnage.

QAT.fact: Qatar is expanding its LNG capacity by about 85 percent by 2030, drawing on the world's largest gas field.

HUN.tagline: Central Europe's battery and car hub
HUN.fact: Hungary is building some of Europe's largest electric-vehicle battery plants, including CATL's factory in Debrecen.

UKR.fact: Ukraine is one of the world's largest exporters of sunflower oil, corn and wheat.

KWT.tagline: Small emirate on vast oil reserves
KWT.fact: Kuwait holds about 6 percent of the world's proven oil reserves, and oil provides around 90 percent of state revenue.

ETH.fact: Ethiopia inaugurated the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam in 2025, Africa's largest hydropower plant.

MAR.fact: Morocco holds about 70 percent of the world's phosphate reserves, vital for fertilizers.

SVK.fact: Slovakia makes more cars per person than any other country, about 180 per 1,000 people.

DOM.fact: The Dominican Republic has been one of Latin America's fastest-growing economies for two decades.

ECU.tagline: Dollarized land of bananas and oil
ECU.fact: Ecuador has used the US dollar as its currency since 2000 and is the world's top banana exporter.

KEN.tagline: East Africa's tech and trade hub
KEN.fact: Kenya pioneered mobile money with M-Pesa, now used by most Kenyan adults.

AGO.fact: Angola left OPEC in 2024 to pump more oil, which still makes up over 90 percent of exports.

OMN.fact: Oman is known as the Gulf's quiet mediator and hosted talks between the US and Iran in 2025.

GTM.fact: Remittances, mainly from the United States, equal about a fifth of Guatemala's GDP.

UZB.fact: Uzbekistan is Central Asia's most populous country, with about 37 million people.

BGR.tagline: Black Sea land, newest euro member
BGR.fact: Bulgaria adopted the euro in January 2026 and has one of the fastest-shrinking populations in the world.

LUX.fact: Nearly half of Luxembourg's workforce commutes daily from France, Belgium and Germany.

VEN.fact: Venezuela holds the world's largest proven oil reserves, about 300 billion barrels, but pumps only around one million barrels a day.

CRI.tagline: Peaceful green nation without an army
CRI.fact: Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948 and generates nearly all its electricity from renewables.

PAN.fact: Panama Canal traffic was cut sharply in 2023-24 when drought lowered Gatun Lake, its freshwater source.

URY.fact: Uruguay generates over 90 percent of its electricity from renewable sources, mostly wind and hydro.

BOL.tagline: Andean land of gas and lithium
BOL.fact: Bolivia holds some of the world's largest lithium resources, about 23 million tonnes, but produces little.

PRY.fact: Paraguay exports much of its share of power from Itaipu, one of the world's largest hydroelectric dams.

HND.fact: Remittances equal about a quarter of Honduras's GDP.

SLV.fact: El Salvador's homicide rate fell to among the lowest in the Americas after a sweeping gang crackdown.

CUB.fact: Cuba suffered repeated nationwide blackouts in 2024 and 2025 as its ageing power plants failed.

TTO.fact: Trinidad and Tobago is one of the world's largest exporters of ammonia and methanol, made from its gas.

HRV.tagline: Adriatic coast of a thousand islands
HRV.fact: Croatia adopted the euro and joined the Schengen area on the same day in January 2023.

SRB.tagline: Balkan crossroads between East and West
SRB.fact: Serbia's population has fallen to about 6.6 million as young people emigrate westward.

LTU.fact: Lithuania hosts a permanent German army brigade, Germany's first such foreign deployment since 1945.

SVN.fact: Floods in 2023 caused Slovenia's costliest disaster, with damage worth about 16 percent of GDP.

LVA.fact: Forests cover over half of Latvia, and wood products are its largest export.

EST.fact: Estonia runs almost all public services online and was the first country to hold nationwide internet voting.

BLR.fact: More than half of Belarus's trade is with Russia, which supplies its oil and gas at discounted prices.

CYP.tagline: Divided island of finance and shipping
CYP.fact: Cyprus has been divided since 1974, with the north run by a Turkish Cypriot administration recognized only by Turkey.

ISL.tagline: Land of fire, ice and fish
ISL.fact: Iceland gets nearly all its electricity and heating from geothermal and hydropower.

AZE.tagline: Land of fire on the Caspian
AZE.fact: Azerbaijan and Armenia initialed a US-brokered peace agreement in August 2025 after decades of conflict.

GEO.tagline: Caucasus crossroads of wine and transit
GEO.fact: Russia occupies about a fifth of Georgia's territory in Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

JOR.tagline: Stable kingdom in a tough neighborhood
JOR.fact: Jordan is one of the most water-scarce countries on Earth and hosts millions of refugees.

BHR.fact: Bahrain's public debt exceeds 120 percent of GDP, the highest among Gulf states.

YEM.tagline: War-torn gateway to the Red Sea
YEM.fact: Yemen imports about 90 percent of its staple food, and over half its people need humanitarian aid.

SYR.tagline: Rebuilding after a long civil war
SYR.fact: The US and EU lifted most sanctions on Syria in 2025 after Assad's fall in December 2024.

LKA.fact: Sri Lanka defaulted on its foreign debt in 2022 and largely completed restructuring under an IMF programme by 2024.

MMR.tagline: Resource-rich land torn by civil war
MMR.fact: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck central Myanmar in March 2025, killing thousands amid an ongoing civil war.

KHM.tagline: Land of Angkor and garment factories
KHM.fact: Garments, footwear and travel goods make up over half of Cambodia's exports.

NPL.tagline: Himalayan land of rivers and remittances
NPL.fact: Remittances from Nepalis working abroad equal over a quarter of the country's GDP.

AFG.fact: Russia became the first country to formally recognize Afghanistan's Taliban government, in July 2025.

PRK.fact: North Korea has sent thousands of troops to fight for Russia, gaining oil, money and technology in return.

TKM.fact: Turkmenistan holds the world's fourth-largest natural gas reserves and sells most of its gas exports to China.

PNG.fact: Papua New Guinea has over 800 languages, more than any other country.

TZA.fact: Gold is Tanzania's largest export, and tourism to Kilimanjaro and Zanzibar is its top service earner.

CIV.fact: Ivory Coast grows about 40 percent of the world's cocoa.

GHA.tagline: West Africa's gold and cocoa land
GHA.fact: Ghana is Africa's largest gold producer and the world's second-largest cocoa grower.

COD.tagline: Vast land of cobalt and rainforest
COD.fact: Congo produces about 70 percent of the world's cobalt, vital for electric-vehicle batteries.

UGA.fact: Uganda is building a crude oil pipeline to Tanzania's coast to export oil from its Lake Albert fields.

CMR.fact: Paul Biya, president since 1982, was declared winner of Cameroon's 2025 election at age 92.

TUN.fact: Tunisia is one of the world's largest olive oil exporters, often second only to Spain.

LBY.fact: Libya holds Africa's largest proven oil reserves but remains split between rival governments in east and west.

SDN.fact: Sudan's war, which began in April 2023, has displaced over 12 million people, the world's largest displacement crisis.

ZMB.fact: A severe 2024 drought cut Zambia's hydropower output, causing blackouts of up to 20 hours a day.

SEN.fact: An audit published in 2025 found Senegal's debt had been badly understated, pushing it above 100 percent of GDP.

ZWE.tagline: Land of minerals and Victoria Falls
ZWE.fact: Zimbabwe launched a gold-backed currency, the ZiG, in 2024 after years of hyperinflation.

MOZ.tagline: Gas giant on the Indian Ocean
MOZ.fact: TotalEnergies' 20 billion dollar LNG project, halted by insurgency in 2021, moved to restart in 2025.

MDG.tagline: Island of vanilla and unique wildlife
MDG.fact: Madagascar grows about 80 percent of the world's natural vanilla.

NER.fact: Niger has one of the world's highest fertility rates, about six children per woman.

MLI.tagline: Sahel gold producer under junta rule
MLI.fact: Jihadist fuel blockades around Bamako in late 2025 caused severe shortages across Mali.

BFA.fact: Gold accounts for over three quarters of Burkina Faso's export earnings.

MWI.fact: Tobacco earns roughly half of Malawi's export income.

TCD.fact: Chad hosts over a million refugees who fled the war in neighbouring Sudan.

SOM.tagline: Horn of Africa's long coastline nation
SOM.fact: Somalia has the longest coastline in mainland Africa, about 3,300 km.

GIN.fact: Guinea began exporting iron ore from Simandou, the world's largest untapped high-grade deposit, in late 2025.
